tasks.title: Doctor remediation core: python row, winget installs, one-confirm batching
tasks.objective: doctor tells the truth about Python and fixes Windows the safe, CI-verifiable way: a required python>=3.10 row mirrored into fast_status, USER-SCOPE winget installs for Git/Python (no harness elevation — a self-elevating installer raises the OS's own single prompt), same-run PATH-refresh convergence on every return path, honest red rows when user-scope cannot complete, and forge next naming doctor --fix. The orchestrated RunAs batch is removed and deferred (D-0021) per decision 0040.
acceptance_criteria: A required python row (version-floored >= 3.10, probing py -3 / python3 / python) joins cmd_doctor AND fast_status (doctor.py:422 two-site agreement pinned by a test); fast_status stays SUBPROCESS-FREE and asserts a version only from the running interpreter's own sys.version_info, other candidates existence-only; the Store zero-length App-Execution-Alias must not be counted as a satisfied interpreter by cmd_doctor's probe (nor legitimate ones wrongly dropped — distinguish by whether it executes, not by zero length); the git row's fix string is platform-branched per _direnv_fix_message (doctor.py:745).

REMOVE the harness-orchestrated RunAs elevation batch entirely (decision 0040 supersedes 0039): _install_git_windows/_install_python_windows resolve winget by canonical-location identity (per-user WindowsApps alias, NO reparse resolve — APPEXECLINK raises WinError 1920) and run USER-SCOPE installs only: winget install --scope user --source winget --silent --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements via direct subprocess.run with an installer-scale timeout (run_quiet's 15s at common.py:17 UNTOUCHED at all sites). No Start-Process -Verb RunAs, no ctypes elevation, no protected-dir enumeration. A package installer that self-elevates raises the OS's own single prompt — not ours.

winget absent -> required red row naming the manual installer URLs (never a bundled download); a user-scope install that cannot complete -> named red row with the manual URL (honest; orchestrated elevation is deferred D-0021).

Same-run convergence: EVERY return path (including partial-install: git queued, python installed) runs _refresh_windows_path() + re-probe before returning, so a successful user-scope install is visible to the same run; the mixed state stays idempotent for a re-run.
phase.py:41 names `./forge doctor --fix` (spec wording).

Tests (argv-recording monkeypatch fakes): user-scope winget argv carries --scope user AND --source winget for each package; NO argv anywhere invokes Start-Process/RunAs; winget-absent and user-scope-failed red rows; partial-install still refreshes+reprobes; python-row/fast_status agreement; env-poisoned PATH/LOCALAPPDATA cannot change the (now non-elevated) install argv. Nothing widens the windows CI selector (D-0020).
Decision 0040 text refined if implementation reveals corrections; status stays proposed.

WOW64 machine-Program-Files — TERMINAL multi-source approach (review contradicted itself on SHGetKnownFolderPath bitness behavior across two rounds; settle by covering ALL documented sources, not betting on one API's WOW64 semantics): _refresh_windows_path() collects native+x86 Program Files candidates from EVERY available source and lets the existing is_dir() filter keep only real ones — (a) %ProgramW6432% env var (Microsoft-documented to always hold the native 64-bit Program Files from any process bitness — the canonical WOW64 answer), (b) %ProgramFiles% and %ProgramFiles(x86)% env vars, (c) FOLDERID_ProgramFiles / FOLDERID_ProgramFilesX86 known folders when they resolve. Remove any reliance on FOLDERID_ProgramFilesX64 (unsupported from a 32-bit process). Reading these env vars here is safe: unelevated PATH-candidate discovery, not a trust boundary; nonexistent dirs are skipped. This is robust by construction regardless of interpreter bitness. Test: a simulated WOW64 env where %ProgramFiles% is the x86 path and %ProgramW6432% the native path finds native Git.
verify_commands: uvx --with pytest python3 -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "doctor_fix or python_row or winget or hook_health"
tasks.reviewer_focus: No harness-orchestrated elevation exists to attack — verify NO Start-Process/RunAs/ctypes-elevation path remains, that installs are user-scope with --source winget pinned, that no user-global config is written, and that env-poisoned PATH/LOCALAPPDATA cannot alter the install argv. run_quiet untouched. POSIX byte-identical except the new python row. fast_status stays subprocess-free. Every return path refreshes+reprobes.

tasks.title: Launcher python3 probe + flow remediation wiring + docs + CI selector
tasks.objective: The remediation reaches users where they enter: forge.cmd probes python3.exe as the last fallback (D-0018), init/adopt/upgrade tails run the fast hook check on Windows and invoke the same one-confirm remediation when red, docs state the Windows story, and the new doctor tests join the explicit windows CI selector.
acceptance_criteria: forge.cmd gains a :python3_fallback label (py -3 -> python -> python3 -> missing) with the same >= 3.10 version gate; the two cross-platform text assertions update in the same change (count of the version-gate string becomes 3; the where-index chain extends to python3) — test_gates.py:2660/2672.

On Windows only, the tails of cmd_init/cmd_adopt/cmd_upgrade run the fast hook check and, when red, invoke doctor's USER-SCOPE remediation (decision 0040 — no harness RunAs; the only possible prompt is a self-elevating installer's own OS prompt); a red result surfaces the named doctor guidance rather than crashing. POSIX flows byte-identical. upgrade.py changes are TAIL-ONLY (post write_manifest, no copy-path change) — any copy-path edit trips the repository-escape escalation tripwire.
docs/getting-started.md's install list gains the Windows prerequisites; new short docs/windows.md documents supported path, remediation flow, WSL2 escape hatch; degraded-mode.md cross-links it.

The windows-hook-gates selector (factory-scaffold.yml, -q stays last, explicit-id list per D-0020) gains the Windows-relevant doctor tests that assert SHIPPING (0040) behavior: test_doctor_python_row_agrees_with_fast_status, test_doctor_fix_reports_winget_absent_as_named_red_row, test_doctor_fix_winget_absent_stays_red_when_tools_appear_after_refresh, test_doctor_fix_nonzero_already_installed_converges_after_refresh, test_doctor_fix_windows_refreshes_native_git_under_wow64, test_doctor_python_row_probes_working_windows_store_alias, plus the new forge.cmd python3-probe test. Do NOT widen to the full suite (D-0020).
Full POSIX suite green; propagation tests from WIN-1 stay green.

Bootstrap: forge.cmd's :missing branch becomes :bootstrap — when no Python 3.10+ is found, resolve winget (canonical location, no reparse), USER-SCOPE install Python (winget --scope user --source winget, NO elevation — a self-elevating installer raises its own OS prompt per 0040), refresh PATH from the known install location, and re-exec the launcher chain ONCE (loop-guard env var); else exit 2 with the named manual fix. Zero typed commands at the true entry point; text assertions updated alongside.

Record-accuracy note (not new work): decision 0040's Decision section is updated to describe the WOW64 multi-source Program Files resolution (ProgramW6432 + FOLDERID_ProgramFiles/X86) that landed in WIN-2.1 — the record catching up to the shipped behavior; no behavior change, docs-only.

Bootstrap placement (review): the Python bootstrap must be reachable on a machine that HAS Git Bash but lacks Python — currently forge.cmd delegates to the sh `forge` launcher as soon as Git Bash is found and exits with its status, and that launcher itself exits 2 when Python is absent, so the bootstrap (only on the native fallback chain) never runs and zero-setup fails in the common 'Git for Windows installed, no separate Python' config. Fix: ensure Python 3.10+ availability BEFORE the Git-Bash handoff (both the sh launcher and the native path require Python to run factory/scripts/forge.py) — probe python up front and run the user-scope bootstrap+PATH-refresh+single-re-exec (loop-guarded) when absent, THEN proceed to shell discovery; a machine with Git Bash but no Python converges without user setup. Test: simulated Git-Bash-present + Python-absent triggers the bootstrap, not an immediate exit 2.
verify_commands: uvx --with pytest python3 -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "forge_cmd or doctor_fix or init or upgrade"
tasks.reviewer_focus: upgrade.py tail-only (tripwire); remediation must not run on POSIX nor mutate vendored files; the selector edit keeps the explicit-id shape; forge.cmd keeps the .exe allowlist and no-call invariants from 0038 — flag any regression of those.

tasks.title: Story-review consolidation: bootstrap state + regressed convergence fixes
tasks.objective: Close the three story-level review findings against committed HEAD: forge.cmd's setlocal-losing-bootstrap-state re-exec bug, and two doctor.py fixes (winget-absent authoritative suppression, PATH-based fast_status python) that regressed during the WOW64 rewrite storm.
acceptance_criteria: forge.cmd: the file's setlocal makes the launcher re-exec perform an implicit endlocal, losing FORGE_PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP_ATTEMPTED and the prepended Python PATH so the bare-Windows path can loop bootstrap forever or fail. Make the guard + refreshed PATH survive the single restart (endlocal & set FORGE_PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP_ATTEMPTED=1 & <invoke>, or set the guard before setlocal) so exactly one bootstrap attempt occurs and PATH persists into the restart.

doctor.py _remediate_windows_prerequisites: RE-ADD the winget-absent authoritative suppression - after the finally re-probe, 'if not winget and git_ok and python_ok:' drop the winget-absent row, so an LTSC/Server box with Git+Python already installed but off-PATH converges GREEN (regressed during WOW64 rounds; verify against git show HEAD:).

doctor.py fast_status: RESTORE the subprocess-free PATH-resolvable python check (any of shutil.which py/python3/python) instead of sys.version_info of the host interpreter, so it agrees with _python_check() under an off-PATH managed interpreter (regressed).

Regression tests pin all three (bootstrap-single-attempt-and-path-persist, winget-absent-converges-green, fast_status-red-when-no-path-python) so a future rewrite cannot silently drop them. Full POSIX suite green; windows-hook-gates selector unchanged.

fast_status python is an OPTIMISTIC subprocess-free preflight HEURISTIC, not a version gate (it runs in the SessionStart hook and must not spawn processes or launch Store aliases): green when the host interpreter is >= 3.10 (forge only runs here because the launcher chain version-gated it) OR when any of py/python3/python resolves on PATH. This resolves both prior findings at once (host-only missed off-PATH names; PATH-only missed version) and is strictly better while staying subprocess-free. _python_check() (subprocess, version-verified) remains the SOLE authority; the earlier 'exact two-site agreement' bar was over-specified and is withdrawn — fast_status may optimistically green a machine doctor would still flag, since forge next only points the user at doctor, which is the accurate backstop. A short comment in fast_status states this heuristic-vs-authoritative contract. Test: fast_status green under an off-PATH >=3.10 host interpreter AND under a PATH py/python3/python; the authoritative version check stays in _python_check only.

Review round (2.3): (1) CI SELECTOR RECONCILE — this task renamed doctor tests the windows-hook-gates selector still references (e.g. the winget-absent test), so CI would fail collecting missing node IDs. Reconcile: update factory-scaffold.yml's explicit selector to the ACTUAL current test names (including the three new 2.3 regression tests), keep the list explicit (D-0020), -q last; every node ID in the selector must exist in test_gates.py. (2) BOOTSTRAP GUARD LEAK — `endlocal & set FORGE_PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP_ATTEMPTED=1 & <invoke>` sets the guard in the CALLER's environment (the restart runs without `call`, so the var persists in the user's shell after forge.cmd returns). Scope the guard to the restarted launcher only (e.g. wrap the re-exec in `cmd /c "set FORGE_PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP_ATTEMPTED=1 & "%~f0" %*"` so the guard lives only in the child cmd, and PATH additions still reach the child) — no guard var leaks into the parent shell; still exactly one bootstrap attempt.
verify_commands: uvx --with pytest python3 -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "forge_cmd or doctor or fast_status or bootstrap or winget"
tasks.reviewer_focus: Verify each of the three against committed HEAD, not the working tree (the regression came from repeated full-file rewrites - recorded lesson). The bootstrap must attempt exactly once. No behavior change beyond the three named items.

tasks.title: Story-review round 2: elevated-run guard + bootstrap re-probe
tasks.objective: Close two story-level findings: refuse to execute the user-writable per-user winget alias when doctor itself is run elevated (privesc guard, consistent with 0040/D-0021), and make forge.cmd's bootstrap refresh PATH and re-probe on winget's 'already installed' nonzero instead of failing to :missing.
acceptance_criteria: doctor.py: before running a user-scope winget install via the per-user %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps alias, detect whether the current process is elevated (ctypes shell32.IsUserAnAdmin or an equivalent token check). When ELEVATED, do NOT execute the user-writable alias (a same-user attacker could replace it -> privesc under admin); instead emit a named red/guidance row telling the user to run 'forge doctor --fix' from a NORMAL (unelevated) prompt, or install manually. When unelevated, behave as today (user-scope install). This upholds 0040 (no privesc) without reviving the deferred machine-winget elevation path (D-0021). No harness RunAs is added.

forge.cmd bootstrap: after the user-scope winget Python install returns, refresh PATH from the known install location and RE-PROBE python (py -3/python/python3 for >=3.10) before deciding; winget's nonzero 'already installed / no applicable upgrade' with Python now on the refreshed PATH must converge, not jump straight to :missing. Still exactly one bootstrap attempt (child-scoped guard unchanged).

Tests: elevated-process simulation asserts the user-writable alias is NOT executed and a named guidance row is emitted; unelevated still installs; forge.cmd bootstrap converges when winget reports already-installed but python is on the refreshed PATH. Full POSIX suite green; CI selector node ids remain valid.

Review round (2.4) — CLOSE THE CLASS, not the instance: (1) AUTHORITATIVE SUPPRESSION covers EVERY provisional Windows remediation row, not only winget-absent: the elevated-run guidance row (and any future provisional row) must also be dropped when the finally-block PATH refresh + authoritative re-probe finds git and python usable — an elevated `forge doctor --fix` on a machine where prerequisites are already present must converge GREEN. Restructure so the post-refresh authority (`if git_ok and python_ok: clear the provisional rows`) applies uniformly, rather than special-casing winget-absent. (2) CI COVERAGE: every new nt-guarded Windows integration test (the bootstrap already-installed test and the elevated-refusal test) joins the explicit windows-hook-gates selector in factory-scaffold.yml (explicit list, -q last, D-0020) so windows-latest actually exercises them — a Windows test that only runs behind os.name=='nt' but is absent from the selector never runs anywhere. Every selector node id must exist.

ELEVATION BOUNDARY — TERMINAL (the privesc class recurred through winget alias, then _python_check re-probe; close it ONCE at the boundary, not per execution path): when doctor detects the current process is elevated (IsUserAnAdmin), the ENTIRE Windows auto-remediation short-circuits at the TOP — no winget install, no _refresh_windows_path(), no _python_check() re-probe of freshly-added per-user directories (all of which could execute user-writable binaries under admin). It returns exactly one named guidance row: run `forge doctor --fix` from a normal (non-admin) prompt. The unelevated path (the common case) is unchanged and fully functional. This upholds 0040 (no privesc) and keeps orchestrated elevation deferred (D-0021) by simply declining to auto-remediate under admin. Test: an elevated run performs ZERO installs and ZERO PATH refresh and emits only the guidance row; the unelevated run still installs/refreshes/converges.
verify_commands: uvx --with pytest python3 -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "doctor or winget or forge_cmd or bootstrap or elevat"
tasks.reviewer_focus: Verify against committed HEAD (recorded rewrite-regression lesson). The elevated guard must not add a RunAs path nor revive D-0021's deferred machine-winget resolution; it only REFUSES the unsafe user-alias-under-admin case honestly. Bootstrap still attempts exactly once.

tasks.title: Close forge.cmd bootstrap elevation path + installed-but-not-found honesty
tasks.objective: Close the last state-changing privesc path (forge.cmd bootstrap executes the user-writable winget alias without an elevation check) and record an honest row when winget succeeds but the tool still cannot run after refresh.
acceptance_criteria: forge.cmd :bootstrap must NOT execute the per-user %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\winget.exe when the launcher is running elevated (a same-user attacker could replace the user-writable alias -> privesc under admin). Detect elevation in batch (e.g. `net session >nul 2>&1` succeeds only when elevated, or `whoami /groups | find "S-1-16-12288"` for High integrity) and when elevated go straight to :missing with the named guidance (run from a normal/unelevated prompt). Unelevated bootstrap behaves as today. This mirrors doctor.py's WIN-2.4 boundary guard into the launcher — the last state-changing path.

doctor.py: when a winget install exits ZERO but the post-refresh authoritative probe still cannot run the tool (unexpected install location / broken install), record a named 'installed but not found' red row instead of silently reporting green — the authoritative probe governs, and a false green is not acceptable.

Tests: elevated forge.cmd bootstrap does NOT run winget and exits to the guidance/missing path; winget-zero-but-tool-still-absent yields a named red row. Full POSIX suite green; every windows CI selector node id exists.

SCOPE NOTE (not this task): the elevated-with-stale-PATH false-refusal usability edge (an elevated doctor showing the refusal row when tools are actually present off a stale PATH) is DEFERRED to D-0022 — correct handling is non-executing status reporting under admin, which needs real-Windows validation; do not attempt it here.

FAIL-CLOSED elevation probe (review — this is the epic's core principle): the batch elevation check must fail CLOSED. Currently `whoami /groups | findstr S-1-16-12288` exposes only findstr's status, so if whoami or findstr cannot run (WDAC/AppLocker, missing binary, pipeline error) the nonzero result is misread as 'unelevated' and winget runs under admin — a fail-OPEN security hole. Restructure so an INDETERMINATE probe (cannot confirm unelevated) is treated as ELEVATED and refuses the winget bootstrap: e.g. capture whoami's own success separately and require a positive 'this is a normal/medium-integrity token' signal before proceeding; any failure or ambiguity goes to :missing with the guidance. Only a definitively-unelevated result runs the bootstrap. Test: simulate whoami/findstr failure and assert the bootstrap does NOT run winget (fails closed to guidance).

CI SELECTOR (review): every nt-guarded Windows test this stage added (the elevated-bootstrap-refusal test, installed-but-not-found test) joins the explicit windows-hook-gates selector in factory-scaffold.yml so windows-latest actually runs them; the list stays explicit (D-0020), -q last, and every node id in the selector must exist in test_gates.py. (Do a full selector audit: no dangling ids, all new WIN-2 Windows tests present.)

SCOPE NOTE (not this task): the elevation probe resolving whoami/findstr through the caller-controllable %SystemRoot% env var — defeatable only by an attacker who both controls forge.cmd's launch environment AND runs it elevated AND supplies a fake whoami crafted to emit the Medium-integrity SID — is DEFERRED into D-0022 (hostile-environment / elevation security-design pass on real Windows). Batch has no non-env System32 resolution; the positive-SID probe already fails closed against a non-matching fake. Do NOT attempt env-hardening here.
verify_commands: uvx --with pytest python3 -m pytest factory/tests/test_gates.py -q -k "forge_cmd or doctor or bootstrap or winget or elevat"

tasks.title: Fix forge.cmd exit-code bugs caught by real-Windows CI
tasks.objective: Make forge.cmd's fallback-chain exit codes correct on real cmd.exe (PR #83 windows-hook-gates caught three failures macOS cannot reproduce) and make the Windows launcher tests deterministic instead of relying on cwd-shadowing against the runner's real Python.
acceptance_criteria: Root-cause and fix the three windows-hook-gates failures (job 94251440123): test_forge_cmd_probes_python3_as_final_fallback (expected exit 2, got 1), test_forge_cmd_bootstrap_refuses_winget_when_elevated (expected 2, got 1), test_forge_cmd_bootstrap_converges_on_already_installed (expected 0, got 1). In each the batch fallback chain reaches a run_python* label and exits 1 (running a failing stub) instead of routing to :missing (exit /b 2) or succeeding (exit 0).

Likely dual root cause — address BOTH: (a) forge.cmd exit-code semantics must be correct on real cmd.exe (reason carefully about `where`/errorlevel/PATHEXT: a `where X` that succeeds then a failing `X -c ...` version probe must route to the next fallback, and when ALL probes fail with the bootstrap guard set it must reach :missing and `exit /b 2` — never fall through to a run_python* label that execs a failed interpreter and returns its exit 1); (b) the Windows tests must be DETERMINISTIC: set the subprocess PATH to ONLY the controlled stub directory plus %SystemRoot%\System32 (for cmd builtins/whoami/findstr/powershell), so the fallback chain cannot resolve the runner's real Python via inherited PATH — do not rely on cwd-shadowing.

Reason from cmd.exe semantics (web search allowed for batch behavior); the fix must make the three named tests pass on windows-latest. Keep the 0038/0040 invariants: .exe-only shell allowlist, no call/RunAs/Start-Process, fail-closed elevation guard, one bootstrap attempt.

POSIX text-assertion portions of the tests still pass on ubuntu; the full POSIX suite stays green. NOTE: neither the orchestrator nor the worker can execute .cmd off Windows — verification is the windows-hook-gates CI job; make the change reason-complete and self-consistent.

CI round 2 remaining failure — test_forge_cmd_bootstrap_converges_on_already_installed expects exit 0 but gets exit 2 (:missing) because forge.cmd's fail-closed elevation guard requires a positive Medium-integrity SID and the windows-latest runner's token is not Medium, so the guard correctly refuses the bootstrap. CORRECTION (my earlier 'whoami PATH stub' instruction was WRONG — forge.cmd invokes %SystemRoot%\System32\whoami.exe by ABSOLUTE path, so a PATH stub is never called): the converge test already regex-patches the FORGE_LOCAL_APP_DATA line in its test_shim; do the same for the elevation-guard block — replace the whoami/findstr Medium-integrity gate (the `if not exist whoami`/`whoami /groups`/`findstr S-1-16-8192 ... goto missing` lines) in the test_shim with a no-op that lets execution fall through to the winget+refresh+re-exec, so the convergence path is exercised in isolation. Do NOT modify forge.cmd itself (the guard is correct; the separate elevated-refuses test verifies it). The other two now-passing tests stay green. Verified via windows CI.
tasks.reviewer_focus: The exit-code routing on real cmd.exe is the crux: trace every path from :python through :missing and the run_* labels; a run_python* label must never be reached with a failed/absent interpreter. Tests must control PATH explicitly. Invariants (allowlist, no call/RunAs, fail-closed) preserved.
